Camila / Elena / Naomi —

Quick ops/finance note from the marketplace playbook side. We support two main invoice patterns for private offers routed through cloud marketplaces:

1) Pass-through invoice (preferred by auditors)
   - Redwood issues a single invoice to the customer showing gross Azure line items and an explicit "Reseller commission — ByteWave" line with negative or zeroed net value as appropriate.
   - ByteWave receives a separate settlement from Redwood (settlement ledger), but the customer's invoice shows the commission as a labeled pass-through.
   - Pros: clean for GL mapping on Helix's side; auditors can see the partner fee.
   - Cons: depends on marketplace SKU packaging; sometimes requires a supplemental agreement to show partner label explicitly on the invoice.

2) Gross-to-net (credit memo flow)
   - Redwood invoices gross, then issues a credit/adjustment representing the reseller commission, which may be processed as a reversal or a separate credit memo to Helix.
   - Pros: simpler from a marketplace SKU perspective in some regions.
   - Cons: requires extra reconciliation on Helix side and can confuse month-end close.

Numbers: based on the 12% ByteWave commission + 5% implementation uplift you referenced, I recommend we present these as two distinct invoice entries: 
- "Reseller commission (ByteWave) — 12%"
- "Channel uplift / Implementation — 5%"

If Helix wants pass-through, we'll need: 1) reseller legal name and tax ID, 2) confirmation that Helix will accept a line-item style invoice (most US customers do).

I've attached a quick commission_calc.xlsx with a sample invoice mock (two pages) showing both pass-through and gross-to-net examples. Naomi — please confirm tax implications and whether we need a localized invoice variation for Helix's state tax rules.

Jordan Blake
